S027-01.notes: Rebuilding eleven times despite failure = persistent; other choices contradict the context.

S027-02.notes: Laying out both interpretations' strengths = even-handed; polemical/partisan are opposites, cursory unsupported. Vocabulary (polemical, cursory) may slow some students.

S027-03.notes: B captures problem plus response. D overstates (shield or turn off, only lights visible from beach); A not mentioned; C a detail/inference. Facts about hatchling phototaxis and lighting ordinances are accurate.

S027-04.notes: Preventing folding increases water loss, directly linking folding to water conservation. A (folding on cool days) and D (no difference with water availability) undercut a water-saving motive; B supports an alternative explanation.

S027-05.notes: Singular possessive for 'the appliance maker' = its. it's = it is; its' nonexistent; their mismatches the singular antecedent (though common in speech, which is the main trap).

flags: minor: 'which' follows '1931,' so the antecedent (the bridge) is slightly separated by the date phrase; acceptable and standard for SAT.
S027-06.notes: Nonrestrictive relative clause after comma requires 'which'; it/this create comma splices; 'that' cannot follow a comma in a nonrestrictive clause.

S027-07.notes: Past practice (for generations, deep plowing) contrasted with current no-till practice = 'Today, however.'

S027-08.notes: Only D gives the cause (red blood cells moving to the liver). C states the effect without explaining why. Facts match published research (Taboada et al., Science 2022: ~2-3x more transparent, ~89% of RBCs pooled in liver).

S027-09.notes: Experiment is an example supporting the general claim. Accurately reflects Appel & Cocroft (2014) Arabidopsis caterpillar-vibration study (glucosinolates/anthocyanins).

flags: minor: D is a superset of A and C (two near-duplicate wrong options), making distractors weak.
minor: 1872 date is the conventional date (Sing-Song, title page 1872; some sources give late 1871) - acceptable.
S027-10.notes: Only B shows the wind known through effects (trembling leaves). Quotations match Rossetti's text.
